\section*{Question 4}

Consider the curve given by \(x^{2}+4 y^{2}=7+3 x y\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Show that \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3 y-2 x}{8 y-3 x}\).
\item[(b)] Show that there is a point \(P\) with \(x\)-coordinate 3 at which the line tangent to the curve at \(P\) is horizontal. Find the \(y\)-coordinate of \(P\).
\item[(c)] Find the value of \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\) at the point \(P\) found in part (b). Does the curve have a local maximum, a local minimum, or neither at the point \(P\) ? Justify your answer.
\item[(a)] \(2 x+8 y y^{\prime}=3 y+3 x y^{\prime}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
(8 y-3 x) y^{\prime} & =3 y-2 x \\
y^{\prime} & =\frac{3 y-2 x}{8 y-3 x}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(\frac{3 y-2 x}{8 y-3 x}=0 ; 3 y-2 x=0\)
When \(x=3,3 y=6\)
\[
y=2
\]
\(3^{2}+4 \cdot 2^{2}=25\) and \(7+3 \cdot 3 \cdot 2=25\)
Therefore, \(P=(3,2)\) is on the curve and the slope is 0 at this point.
\item[(c)] \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{(8 y-3 x)\left(3 y^{\prime}-2\right)-(3 y-2 x)\left(8 y^{\prime}-3\right)}{(8 y-3 x)^{2}}\)
At \(P=(3,2), \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{(16-9)(-2)}{(16-9)^{2}}=-\frac{2}{7}\).
Since \(y^{\prime}=0\) and \(y^{\prime \prime}<0\) at \(P\), the curve has a local maximum at \(P\).
\end{itemize}

\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \\ 1: \text { shows slope is } 0 \text { at }(3,2) \\ 1: \text { shows }(3,2) \text { lies on curve }\end{array}\right.\)
